articles.title: Thousands join Berlin’s Peace Days to support antimilitarism and solidarity
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: On August 28-30, over 5,000 people gathered in Berlin for the UZ-Friedenstage – Unsere Zeit’s Peace Days – the bi-annual festival organized by the German Communist Party (DKP). The program included political discussions, concerts, readings, and workshops, representing notable growth since the last edition in 2024. The festival drew a cross-generational audience of trade unionists, activists, students, authors, ambassadors, renters’ associations, and communist and workers’ parties from around the world. The Peace Days took place against the backdrop of Germany’s militarization and the government’s measures against workers’ rights, social provision, and democratic participation. articles.title: Tanzanian opposition leader ordered to defend himself in treason trial
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Tanzania’s High Court has ruled that Chadema party chairman Tundu Lissu must present a formal defense in his treason trial , a charge that carries a maximum penalty of death if he is convicted. The ruling is not a conviction. At this stage of a criminal trial, the court is only deciding whether the prosecution has produced evidence that, left unanswered, could support a conviction. It is not a final determination of guilt, nor a detailed assessment of witness credibility. From “No Reforms, No Election” to a treason charge The case goes back to Chadema’s nationwide “No Reforms, No Election” campaign, which called for changes to Tanzania’s electoral system ahead of the October 2025 general election. articles.title: With Xi, Putin, and Modi in attendance, SCO condemns US economic warfare
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: The 26th annual summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) concluded in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on Tuesday, September 1. This years’ summit was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, among others. At the conclusion of the summit, member countries adopted the Bishkek Declaration , which reiterates the common resolve of the SCO to work against all forms of hegemonic practices in world politics and create a truly democratic and equitable world order. The declaration also condemned the growing use of unilateral coercive measures or sanctions by certain countries to achieve their geopolitical goals

articles.author: Peoples Health Dispatch
articles.content_excerpt: On July 21, 2026, 25-year-old intern doctor Muhammad Zulfikar Drakel was found dead in his boarding room in Metro, Lampung. He was the sixth Indonesian medical intern to die on duty this year alone. These physicians are the most visible casualties of a much larger epidemic, one that has engulfed health workers across the 17,000 islands archipelago. Less than a week later, intern doctor Siti Zahra Maghfira jumped from her family’s apartment balcony while her parents were out. articles.author: BreakThrough News
articles.content_excerpt: On Sunday, August 30, Colombia’s newly inaugurated president, the far-right Abelardo de la Espriella, announced he was canceling the peace negotiations with several armed groups which had started during the previous administration led by Gustavo Petro. articles.title: Cuando la montaña se derrumbó: Los detalles de la inundación más mortífera del Himalaya en Nepal
articles.author: Madhab Pant
articles.content_excerpt: Read in English here Aproximadamente a las 8:30 a. m. del 26 de agosto de 2026, un muro de agua, lodo, hielo y enormes rocas descendió con estruendo por el Lhende Khola hacia los sistemas fluviales del Bhotekoshi y el Trishuli. La oleada se produjo sin que hubiera lluvias locales ni sonaran las sirenas de alerta, tomando por sorpresa a media mañana a comunidades fronterizas como Timure. articles.title: US resumes airstrikes on Iran after month-long pause
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: The military confrontation between the United States and Iran came back to the fore after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on its Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, on Sunday, August 30. US Central Command (CENTCOM) claimed that the attack on Larak was launched to prevent Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) from laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz. However, an Iranian military source debunked CENTCOM’s claim as “fantasy and story making.” The offensive marks the first US strike since July 29. articles.title: U.S. Claims Majority Control of Venezuela’s Oil Reserves

articles.title: Amid Severe Water Crisis & Drought, Puerto Rico Marks 10 Years of “La Junta” Oversight
articles.content_excerpt: Juan Carlos Dávila reports from Puerto Rico as the island grapples with a severe water crisis. A record-breaking drought has led to severe shortages and a system of water rationing that residents say could have been prevented by better infrastructure maintenance. Climate scientists have warned for years that changing weather conditions in the Caribbean are likely to exacerbate existing infrastructure failings, but rather than address the root cause of the water shortage, explains Dávila, a pattern of government inaction and failed public services is used to justify increasing privatization. Puerto Rico’s water woes come 10 years after the United States passed the bankruptcy law PROMESA to restructure the U.S. territory’s debt, installing an unelected board colloquially known as “La Junta”

articles.title: September 2026 (Volume 78, Number 4)
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: Taking as a starting point two classic works of the mid-nineteenth century—Benjamin Disraeli’s Sybil; or the Two Nations and Frederick Engels’s The Condition of the Working Class in England —this month’s “Notes from the Editors” explores the way both authors articulated the plight of workers in their own era, drawing key parallels to our own time. The similarities are particularly conspicuous when examining the so-called affordability crisis, exposing the regime of social murder that accompanies the increasing polarization of economic life. articles.title: India’s Ruling Classes and the Global Crisis
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: In September’s Review of the Month, the Research Unit for Political Economy delves into how the crisis pervading the world system, on stark display in the tech sector, global finance, and the sphere of production, lays bare the longstanding vulnerabilities of the Indian economy. As the contradictions in the neoliberal phase become unmistakable, the authors write, it is necessary to take a class-based approach to resolving the questions of how to bring about key questions regarding the productive life and development of India. articles.title: José Carlos Mariátegui and Local Traditions of Struggle
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: The relationship between Marxism and other revolutionary traditions is a key question for our time. If we approach the issue incorrectly, we risk Eurocentrism and underrecognizing Marxism’s role in the Global South contexts where it is most vital and active. This article examines and extends José Carlos Mariátegui’s dialectical approach to the issue, which demonstrates how Marxism is not diluted but strengthened through engagement with the thought and practice of existing struggles, while those struggles can, in turn, gain greater depth and groundedness through the same relationship. The post José Carlos Mariátegui and Local Traditions of Struggle appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.title: Beyond Scarcity: Thomas Sowell and the Limits of Neoclassical Economics
articles.author: Jamil Jonna
articles.content_excerpt: Through the work of neoclassical economist Thomas Sowell, Elliot Goodell Ugalde dissects the orthodox view that takes for granted that scarcity is at the center of economic life. In a world of various kinds of surpluses, Goodell argues, the idea that scarcity is the only organizing principle of our economic is inadequate to describe the complex interactions of institutions, history, and social power that make up economic organization under capitalism. The post Beyond Scarcity: Thomas Sowell and the Limits of Neoclassical Economics appeared first on Monthly Review .

articles.content_excerpt: In this 1980 talk by Joan Robinson, first published in MR in 1983, the economist painted a stark picture of global arms race fueled by military capitalism and imperialism. The important question,” she urged, “is not whether the rate of inflation is high or low or can be brought under control but whether our generation will succeed in destroying the world…. articles.author: Jamil Jonna

The book, Buhle writes, is a window onto “the antinomies of nineteenth-century Jewish life”—including the growing movement against Zionism and for socialism among Eastern European Jews. This authors, Buhle notes, also tells the story of Jewish communists in Britain, the United States, and beyond, taking into account the wide sweep of Jewish left activity globally, situating the present struggles against genocide in Palestine squarely within the legacy of radical Jews everywhere.
